cheatsheet.title: Cheat Sheet
cheatsheet.tab.ores.legend: The big number is the best height to dig at. A brighter bar means more ore.
cheatsheet.tab.ores.legend.bonus: Striped: extra ore in one biome
cheatsheet.tab.ores.flat: Just as common anywhere from Y %s to %s
cheatsheet.tab.ores.bonus.badlands: Lots of extra gold from Y %s to %s
cheatsheet.tab.ores.bonus.emerald: Emeralds only here, best at Y %s
cheatsheet.tab.ores.bonus.dripstone.deta: Same heights as copper: Y %s to %s
cheatsheet.tab.ores.bonus.deltas.detail: Nether gold and quartz from Y %s to %s
cheatsheet.tab.ores.bonus.debris: Ancient debris forms large veins from Y %s to %s and small ones from Y %s to %s
cheatsheet.tab.enchantments.section.titl: %s · %s: not from the enchanting table · %s: curse
cheatsheet.tab.enchantments.curse: Curse: a drawback, not a bonus
cheatsheet.tab.enchantments.anvil_only: The enchanting table doesn't give it on this item, so put a book on it with an anvil
cheatsheet.tab.enchantments.table_only: The enchanting table gives it only on %s; for the rest, use an anvil
cheatsheet.tab.enchantments.librarians: Librarians can sell it as a book
cheatsheet.tab.enchantments.anvil_cost: Anvil cost per level: %s from a book, %s from an item
cheatsheet.tab.enchantments.anvil.title: Anvil: several books on one tool
cheatsheet.tab.enchantments.anvil.step.1: Book 1 + book 2 → one book with both.
cheatsheet.tab.enchantments.anvil.step.2: Book 3 + book 4 → another book with two.
cheatsheet.tab.enchantments.anvil.step.3: Join those two books → one book with all four.
cheatsheet.tab.enchantments.anvil.step.4: Pickaxe on the left + that book on the right → pickaxe with all four.
cheatsheet.tab.enchantments.anvil.merge: Both pieces have an extra cost of %s: you pay %s levels + the enchantments of the book on the right. The new book's extra cost: %s.
cheatsheet.tab.enchantments.anvil.final: Pickaxe (extra cost 0) + book (extra cost %s): you pay %s levels + the book's enchantments; the pickaxe's own are free. Its extra cost is now %s.
cheatsheet.tab.enchantments.anvil.counte: Every item or book carries a hidden counter of how many times it has been through the anvil. Each time you use it, it gets more expensive to use again: it costs %s, then %s extra levels. If an operation costs %s levels or more, the anvil says “%s” and won't let you do it.
cheatsheet.tab.enchantments.anvil.trick: Trick: don't let any item go through the anvil many times. You do it by joining things in pairs.
cheatsheet.tab.enchantments.anvil.one_by: Don't put the books on the pickaxe one by one: around the %sth–%sth you get “%s”.
cheatsheet.tab.enchantments.anvil.more_b: More books? Same idea: join them in pairs, then the pairs, and so on; the tool goes last. %s books: %s levels of extra cost in all, instead of %s one by one.
cheatsheet.tab.enchantments.anvil.cost: At each step you pay the extra cost of both pieces plus the enchantments of the piece on the RIGHT.
cheatsheet.tab.enchantments.anvil.cost.d: From %s levels the anvil refuses: %s (Survival only). The enchantments of the piece on the LEFT are free.

Less fire damage, and you burn for less time
Arrows set targets on fire
More drops from ores, crops and other blocks
Turns water into ice under your feet; no damage from magma blocks
Extra damage to aquatic mobs
Shoot without using up normal arrows (you need one)

Mobs drop more loot
The thrown trident comes back to you
More treasure and less junk when fishing

Arrows deal more damage
Less damage from arrows, tridents and other projectiles
Less damage from almost everything

cheatsheet.tab.potions.into_awkward: Add it to an Awkward Potion
cheatsheet.tab.potions.fuel.tooltip: It's the brewing stand's fuel, and one blaze powder lasts 20 brews
cheatsheet.tab.potions.modifier.redstone: Makes the potion last longer. Not on a potion already made stronger.
cheatsheet.tab.potions.modifier.glowston: Makes the potion stronger but shorter. Not on a potion already made longer.
cheatsheet.tab.potions.modifier.spider_e: Turns the potion into its opposite, usually keeping its upgrade.
cheatsheet.tab.potions.modifier.gunpowde: Turns any potion into a splash potion you can throw.
cheatsheet.tab.potions.modifier.dragon_b: Turns a splash potion into a lingering one that leaves an effect cloud. Fill glass bottles with dragon's breath during the Ender Dragon fight.
cheatsheet.tab.trims.where.trail_ruins: Brushing suspicious gravel in trail ruins
cheatsheet.tab.trims.where.trial_vault: Vault, opened with a trial key, or a reward chest
cheatsheet.tab.trims.where.ominous_vault: Ominous vault, opened with an ominous trial key
cheatsheet.tab.discs.section: Each disc: where to find it and how long it plays
cheatsheet.tab.discs.how.creeper_killed_: Creeper killed by a skeleton (any kind)
cheatsheet.tab.discs.how.trial_vault: Vault, opened with a trial key, or a reward chest
cheatsheet.tab.discs.how.ominous_vault: Ominous vault, opened with an ominous trial key
cheatsheet.tab.discs.how.trial_pots: Decorated pots in trial chamber corridors
cheatsheet.tab.discs.how.trail_ruins: Brushing suspicious gravel in trail ruins
cheatsheet.tab.discs.how.ghast_own_fireb: Ghast killed by a fireball you hit back
cheatsheet.tab.discs.how.chicken_jockey: Baby zombie riding a chicken, killed by you
cheatsheet.tab.dyes.section: Sources and mixes of each dye
cheatsheet.tab.villagers.legend: Each level adds up to %s trades picked at random from its row. Hover a trade for details.
cheatsheet.tab.villagers.kind.enchanted_: Enchantments are random, and better ones cost more
The enchantment is random. Higher levels cost more, and treasure ones cost double (Mending: %s)
cheatsheet.tab.villagers.bartering.pay: Give it to a piglin and it throws back one random item
cheatsheet.tab.villagers.trader.note: It shows up near you with two llamas. On each visit it picks offers at random from every row.
cheatsheet.tab.food.title: Most filling first
cheatsheet.tab.food.always: Can be eaten even when full
cheatsheet.tab.food.teleports: Teleports you up to %s blocks away
cheatsheet.tab.food.stew: Effect depends on the flower used
cheatsheet.tab.food.legend.note: Saturation is used up before hunger: the higher it is, the longer you stay full. Hover a food for its effects.
cheatsheet.tab.beacon.pyramid.secondary: Or level II of the primary effect
cheatsheet.tab.beacon.payment.note: After you leave the range, the effect lasts up to %s s at level 1 or %s s at level 4.
cheatsheet.tab.beacon.conduit.ring.detai: The rings of frame blocks go around the conduit, facing all three ways. It takes %s to activate it and %s for the full frame
cheatsheet.tab.beacon.conduit.attack: Also attacks hostile mobs in water or rain within %s blocks
cheatsheet.tab.beacon.conduit.power: It lets you breathe underwater, see in the dark and mine faster underwater
cheatsheet.tab.beacon.conduit.rule: Only blocks on these 3 rings count; any %s will do.
cheatsheet.tab.beacon.conduit.water: The conduit sits, waterlogged, in the middle of a 3×3×3 of water. Works on players in water or rain.
cheatsheet.tab.beacon.source.buried_trea: Buried treasure: follow a map from a shipwreck or ocean ruins
cheatsheet.tab.beacon.source.drowned: Drowned holding one (%s%% spawn with it)
cheatsheet.tab.beacon.source.sea_lantern: Breaking a sea lantern without Silk Touch
cheatsheet.tab.beacon.conduit.guide.titl: Building a conduit, step by step
cheatsheet.tab.beacon.conduit.guide.step: Place the conduit in the middle of a 3×3×3 cube full of water.
Place a %s×%s square around it, flat, with %s blocks. Any %s blocks of the rings already activate it.
Place the same square upright. That makes %s blocks in all.
Repeat it upright the other way, for %s blocks. It reaches %s blocks and attacks hostile mobs in water or rain within %s blocks.
cheatsheet.tab.beacon.conduit.guide.rang: Range for each number of frame blocks:
cheatsheet.tab.farming.sugar_cane.water: Sugar cane needs water (or frosted ice) right beside the block it stands on, not diagonally.
cheatsheet.tab.farming.sugar_cane.cane: Plant it on dirt, grass, mud, moss or sand. It grows up to %s blocks tall. If you cut it above the bottom block, it grows back.
cheatsheet.tab.farming.sugar_cane.free: With no water beside it there can be no cane, so it stays free to walk on.
cheatsheet.tab.farming.sugar_cane.zoom: Unlike other crops, sugar cane can only be placed right beside water, not diagonally. Fitting all the crosses together gives the most efficient shape. Layout 3 is easier to walk through; 4 has only %s more canes, though it fills the whole field.
cheatsheet.tab.farming.field.caption: Water reaches %s blocks · alternate rows ×2
cheatsheet.tab.farming.field.water: One water block hydrates farmland up to %s blocks away, which gives a %s×%s field. It must be at the same height or one block higher.
cheatsheet.tab.farming.field.crop: A crop with the same crop beside it in both directions (or diagonally) grows at half speed. So rows of different crops grow twice as fast as a field of one.
cheatsheet.tab.farming.stems.title: Pumpkins and melons
cheatsheet.tab.farming.stems.caption: A free block beside each stem
cheatsheet.tab.farming.stems.water: Keeps the farmland of the stems on both sides hydrated.
cheatsheet.tab.farming.stems.stem: The fruit grows on a free block beside the stem (dirt, grass, mud, moss or farmland). Leave one for every stem. The stem itself grows on farmland.
cheatsheet.tab.farming.stems.fruit: The fruit grows here. Harvest it and the stem grows another.
cheatsheet.tab.farming.stems.free: This block stays free because the fruit will grow here.
cheatsheet.tab.farming.cactus.caption: Nothing solid on its sides · on sand
cheatsheet.tab.farming.cactus.cactus: It breaks if a solid block or lava touches its sides, even another cactus, so plant them in a checkerboard. It needs sand or red sand below and grows up to %s blocks tall.
cheatsheet.tab.farming.cactus.sand: Keep the air above it free, because a cactus there would break the ones beside it.
cheatsheet.tab.farming.place.wandering_t: Two trader llamas come with each wandering trader
cheatsheet.tab.farming.place.warm_ocean_: Sniffer eggs come from brushing suspicious sand in warm ocean ruins
cheatsheet.tab.farming.get.lure: It follows you if you hold its food, or you can tie it to a lead.
cheatsheet.tab.farming.get.cow: It follows you if you hold wheat, or you can tie it to a lead. If you shear a mooshroom, it becomes a cow.
cheatsheet.tab.farming.get.chicken: It follows you if you hold seeds. A thrown egg can hatch a chick.
cheatsheet.tab.farming.get.tame_by_ridin: Mount it with an empty hand until it stops throwing you off; feeding it first helps.
cheatsheet.tab.farming.get.llama: Mount it with an empty hand until it stops throwing you off; wheat or hay bales help.
cheatsheet.tab.farming.get.tame_with_ite: Feed it the items shown until hearts appear.
cheatsheet.tab.farming.get.ocelot: It can't be tamed. To gain its trust, stand still holding raw fish and feed it.
cheatsheet.tab.farming.get.fox: It runs from players. If you breed two foxes, their cub trusts you.
cheatsheet.tab.farming.get.bee: Break its nest with Silk Touch to move the bees. If you hold flowers, they follow you.
cheatsheet.tab.farming.get.turtle: It follows you if you hold seagrass. Its eggs hatch on sand.
cheatsheet.tab.farming.get.frog: Catch a tadpole in a water bucket and let it out. It becomes a frog after 20 minutes.
cheatsheet.tab.farming.get.axolotl: It spawns underwater, over clay. Catch it in a water bucket.
cheatsheet.tab.farming.get.camel: It's born tame, so just saddle it.
cheatsheet.tab.farming.get.sniffer: Place the egg. It hatches in 20 minutes, or in 10 on a moss block.
cheatsheet.tab.farming.get.strider: It follows you if you hold warped fungus. It walks on lava.
cheatsheet.tab.farming.get.hoglin: It's hostile, so move it with a lead. In the Overworld it turns into a zoglin.
cheatsheet.tab.farming.ride.saddle: Saddle it to ride and steer it.
cheatsheet.tab.farming.ride.carrot_on_a_: Saddle it and steer it with a carrot on a stick.
cheatsheet.tab.farming.ride.warped_fungu: Saddle it and steer it with a warped fungus on a stick.
cheatsheet.tab.farming.ride.not_steered: It's ridden without a saddle, but it can't be steered. If you lead one, the llamas nearby follow. Carpets decorate it.
cheatsheet.tab.farming.variant.grows: A tadpole that grows up in %s becomes this frog
cheatsheet.tab.farming.variant.how.light: A red mooshroom struck by lightning turns brown, and back.
cheatsheet.tab.farming.variant.how.moosh: Two mooshrooms of the same colour may have a calf of the other colour
cheatsheet.tab.farming.variant.how.brown: Thrown brown eggs, laid by warm chickens, hatch warm chicks.
cheatsheet.tab.farming.variant.how.blue_: Thrown blue eggs, laid by cold chickens, hatch cold chicks.
cheatsheet.tab.farming.variant.how.toast: Name any rabbit "Toast" with a name tag.
cheatsheet.tab.farming.variant.how.kille: It never spawns naturally, only with commands. It attacks players and wolves.
cheatsheet.tab.farming.variant.how.swamp: Every cat in a swamp hut is black.
cheatsheet.tab.farming.variant.how.full_: It appears in villages only at full moon, as one more coat
cheatsheet.tab.farming.variant.how.gene: In wild pandas, it shows when it is the main gene
cheatsheet.tab.farming.variant.how.reces: It's recessive, so it shows only when both genes are this one
cheatsheet.tab.farming.variant.how.tadpo: A tadpole that grows up in any other biome becomes this frog.
cheatsheet.tab.farming.variant.note.inhe: Babies take the look of one parent.
cheatsheet.tab.farming.variant.note.shee: Lambs mix their parents' colours when the dyes mix. Dye a sheep any colour.
cheatsheet.tab.farming.variant.note.chic: Chicks take the look of one parent; a thrown egg hatches the chick of its colour.
cheatsheet.tab.farming.variant.note.rabb: Babies take a parent's look, but 1 in 20 takes the look of the biome.
cheatsheet.tab.farming.variant.note.goat: One goat in 50 is a screaming goat. It looks the same, but it screams and drops horns with other sounds.
cheatsheet.tab.farming.variant.note.hors: There are 5 random markings: none, white stockings, white field, white dots and black dots. Foals take a parent's coat, but 1 in 9 gets a random one.
cheatsheet.tab.farming.variant.note.llam: Trader llamas have the same coats. Babies take the coat of one parent.
cheatsheet.tab.farming.variant.note.pand: A panda carries two genes, one from each parent (sometimes a random one).
cheatsheet.tab.farming.variant.note.frog: It isn't inherited, because the biome where the tadpole grows up decides it.
cheatsheet.tab.farming.variant.note.axol: Babies take a parent's colour, but 1 in 1200 is blue.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.empty: None yet. The + button saves your own commands, and the star on any built-in one copies it here.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.dangerous: It asks before running, because it can destroy or remove things.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.button.chat: Open in the chat to edit it
cheatsheet.tab.commands.button.add_full: Full: delete one to add another
cheatsheet.tab.commands.favourite.full: My commands is full (%s). Delete one first.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.combo.permission: Running several commands at once needs cheats on or operator permission.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.form.name: Name
cheatsheet.tab.commands.form.hint: Write one per line and they run in order. The slash is optional. It holds up to %s lines of %s characters.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.teleport: Teleport yourself to X Y Z coordinates: change the three numbers.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.give: Give yourself a stack of an item: change the item and the amount.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.night_visio: See in the dark until you clear your effects, without particles.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.regeneratio: Heal very fast for one minute.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.levels: Add 30 experience levels: enough for the best enchantments.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.difficulty: Set the difficulty: peaceful, easy, normal or hard.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.spawnpoint: Respawn where you stand, without a bed.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.keep_invent: Keep your items and experience when you die.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.stop_daylig: Freeze the sun and moon where they are (true starts it again).
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.stop_weathe: The weather never changes by itself (true starts it again).
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.no_mob_grie: Creepers and other mobs no longer break or move blocks.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.no_fire_spr: Fire no longer spreads or burns blocks away.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.no_phantoms: Phantoms stop appearing when you skip sleep.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.immediate_r: Respawn at once, without the death screen.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.fill: Fill a 10 x 5 x 10 box beside you with stone, replacing what is there.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.fill_hollow: Puts glass walls, floor and roof around you, and everything inside becomes air.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.fill_outlin: Puts stone brick walls, floor and roof around you and keeps the inside.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.fill_replac: Turn all stone around you into glass, to see caves and ores.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.fill_destro: Break the blocks around you as if mined, dropping them as items.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.flatten: Remove every block from your feet to 20 blocks above them, 15 blocks around you.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.remove_wate: Remove the water within 15 blocks to each side and 10 up and down.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.remove_lava: Remove the lava within 15 blocks to each side and 10 up and down.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.clone: Copy the blocks around you 14 blocks east, replacing what is there.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.setblock: Put a block under your feet: change the block.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.barrier_flo: Puts an invisible barrier floor under you, only where there is air.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.world_borde: Make the world border 1000 blocks wide.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.sword: A netherite sword with Sharpness V, Looting III, Fire Aspect II, Knockback II, Sweeping Edge III, Unbreaking III and Mending.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.pickaxe: A netherite pickaxe with Efficiency V, Fortune III, Unbreaking III and Mending.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.helmet: A netherite helmet with Protection IV, Respiration III, Aqua Affinity, Unbreaking III and Mending.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.chestplate: A netherite chestplate with Protection IV, Unbreaking III and Mending.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.leggings: Netherite leggings with Protection IV, Swift Sneak III, Unbreaking III and Mending.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.boots: Netherite boots with Protection IV, Feather Falling IV, Depth Strider III, Soul Speed III, Unbreaking III and Mending.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.mace: A mace with Density V, Wind Burst III, Unbreaking III and Mending.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.rockets: 64 firework rockets with the longest flight, for the elytra.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.player_head: The head of a player: change the name.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.potion: A potion of speed, jump boost and regeneration for five minutes.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.command_blo: A block that runs a command when powered.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.debug_stick: Changes a block's state: stairs' shape, a fence's sides, a door's hinge.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.barrier: Invisible blocks you cannot walk through; only creative mode can break them.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.light: Invisible blocks that give light, so no torches are needed.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.structure_v: Marks the spots a structure block leaves untouched when it places.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.locate_vill: Show where the nearest village is; click the coordinates for a teleport command.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.locate_biom: Show the nearest cherry grove: change the biome.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.go_nether: Teleport to the matching spot in the Nether, on safe ground under the roof.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.go_end: Teleport onto the End's main island, near its centre.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.go_overworl: Teleport to the matching spot in the Overworld, on the surface.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.gold_under_: It runs as every player, at their feet, and puts a gold block under them.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.kill_items: Remove every item lying on the ground in loaded chunks.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.kill_monste: Kill the common hostile mobs within 64 blocks, except named ones.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.frozen_mob: Creates a zombie that never moves, attacks or despawns, like a statue.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.invisible_s: An invisible armour stand with arms, to show armour or items.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.villager_tr: A villager that stays put and trades a diamond for an emerald and an emerald for dirt.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.tellraw: Send everyone a gold, bold message: change the text.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.seed: Show the world's seed; click it to copy it.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.mob_health: Show the health of the nearest mob.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.particles: Show heart particles over your head: change the particle.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.sound: Play the level-up sound to yourself: change the sound.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.lightning: Strike lightning five blocks in front of you.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.enchant: Add Sharpness V to the item in your hand: change the enchantment and level.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.fast_growth: Crops, saplings and grass grow about 30 times faster (3 is the default).
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.full_kit: Everything at once: maxed netherite armour, sword and tools, bow and arrows, shield, food, a totem, elytra and rockets.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.armour_kit: The four netherite armour pieces with their best enchantments.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.tools_kit: Netherite pickaxes (Fortune and Silk Touch), axe, shovel and hoe, and shears, all maxed.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.weapons_kit: Maxed sword, bow, crossbow, trident and mace, a shield and 64 arrows.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.food_kit: Golden carrots, steak, golden apples, enchanted golden apples and a totem of undying.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.elytra_kit: An elytra with Unbreaking III and Mending, and 64 long-flight rockets.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.builder_kit: Debug stick, light blocks, barriers and structure voids.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.build_world: Keeps the world always day, with no rain and no mobs spawning naturally, the usual setup for building or recording.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.friendly_ru: Turns on keep inventory and instant respawn, and turns off mob griefing, fire spread and phantoms.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.quiet_comma: Commands stop announcing their results in the chat, so the screen stays clean for videos.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.flat_area: Clear 31 x 31 blocks around you, 21 high, and lay a grass floor.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.default_rul: Put back the default of every game rule the other world combos change.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.kill_dragon: Run it in the End. It kills the end crystals and the Ender Dragon, and the exit portal opens as after a fight.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.kill_wither: Kill every loaded Wither and its flying skulls.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.clean_groun: Remove the dropped items, experience orbs and arrows lying in loaded chunks.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.reset_playe: Empties your inventory, removes effects and experience and puts you back in survival, for a clean start to a test.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.invincible: Gives you Resistance V, fast regeneration, fire resistance, water breathing and saturation until you clear them.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.miner: Gives you Haste II and night vision until you clear them.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.explorer: Gives you Speed II, Jump Boost II and night vision until you clear them.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.underwater: Gives you water breathing, Dolphin's Grace, Conduit Power and night vision until you clear them.
cheatsheet.tab.commands.desc.recording: Sets spectator mode, night vision and a still, sunny noon, for screenshots and videos (F1 hides the HUD).
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.card.ticks.title: Ticks
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.plates.wood.what: anything on it activates it, such as players, mobs, items or arrows. It gives a signal of %s.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.plates.stone.wha: players, mobs and armour stands activate it, but items don't. It gives a signal of %s.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.plates.light.wha: the signal rises 1 per entity on it, up to %s (with %s entities).
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.plates.heavy.wha: it gives 1 with the first entity and rises 1 per 10 more, up to %s (with %s entities).
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.plates.timing: A plate stays on while something is on it, and at least %s s after a touch (weighted: %s s).
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.comparator.compa: gives the signal at its input end, or 0 if a side signal is stronger.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.comparator.subtr: it gives the input signal minus the strongest side signal.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.comparator.reads: it is the end with two torches, opposite the single front torch. A container placed there (or a composter, a cake…) gives a signal by how full it is, even through one solid block.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.comparator.examp: Each number is the signal strength at that spot. The signal comes in from the left and goes out on the right, and the number at the top is what arrives from the side.
%s comes in and %s arrives from the side, so the comparator lets the %s through.
%s comes in, but %s arrives from the side. Because the side is stronger, %s comes out. If %s or less arrived from the side, the %s would come out.
With the front torch lit, the comparator subtracts what arrives from the side. %s comes in and %s arrives from the side, so %s − %s = %s comes out.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.table.title: Items for each signal (items stacking to 64)
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.table.formula: The signal is 1 + ⌊14 × fullness⌋, or 0 when empty. Fullness is the average over all slots of each slot's items divided by its stack size.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.table.stacks: Hover a number to see how many it takes if they stack to 16 or don't stack.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.table.crafter: The crafter counts slots, not items. It gives 1 per slot holding an item or disabled, however many items are in it, and %s at most.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.table.crafter.ce: %s slots with an item or disabled
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.table.minecarts: A chest minecart counts as %s slots and a hopper minecart as %s. The comparator reads the detector rail they stand on.
Each slot with an item counts as 1, whether it holds 1 item or a full stack. For example, with %s disabled, %s items, one per slot, are enough to reach %s.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.roof.title: Roof bedrock by height
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.roof.note: Each block is decided on its own. Above the roof you walk at Y %s, and below Y %s there is no bedrock, only netherrack.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.mining.title: Does it mine a piston instantly?
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.mining.note: With your feet on the ground. In the air or underwater, mining is much slower.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.special.cake: gives %s whole and loses %s per slice eaten.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.special.lectern: gives 1 on the first page and %s on the last, by 1 + ⌊14 × (page − 1) ÷ (pages − 1)⌋.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.special.jukebox: gives %s to %s by disc (see the Discs tab).
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.special.item_fra: gives 1 to %s by the item's rotation.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.special.cauldron: gives 1 to %s by level, and %s with lava.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.special.end_port: gives %s with an eye and 0 without.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.special.shelf: is read from behind. The left slot is worth %s, the middle %s and the right %s, and they add up.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.special.chiseled: gives 1 to %s by the slot used last, left to right from the top row, and 0 if never used.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.special.copper_b: gives %s when lit and 0 when off.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.special.sculk_se: gives the last vibration's frequency, up to %s, only while active.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.special.creaking: gives %s with its creaking right beside it, falling to 0 at %s blocks. Without a creaking it gives 0.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.special.command_: gives how many times its command worked on its last run, usually 1, or 0 if it failed.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.sculk.signal.wha: it is %s up close and drops with distance, by %s − ⌊15 × distance ÷ range⌋. It is at least 1.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.sculk.timing.wha: a vibration takes %s s per block to arrive. The sensor stays on %s s (calibrated, %s s), then is deaf %s s.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.sculk.wool.what: it blocks vibrations passing through it. Wool and carpets make none when walked on, placed or broken. If you sneak, your footsteps aren't heard.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.sculk.calibrated: a signal into the side that faced you when you placed it makes it hear only that frequency. With no signal, it hears everything.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.sculk.frequencie: A comparator reads the vibration's frequency
Shooting, finishing using an item, goat horns
Elytra gliding, taking off gear, mob actions
Getting off a mount, putting on gear
Mounting, shearing, using an item on a mob
Closing chests and doors, switching off, unhooking tripwire
Opening chests and doors, switching on, lighting TNT, note blocks
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.ticks.units: A game tick lasts %s s (%s per second). A redstone tick is %s game ticks, or %s s.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.ticks.torch.what: delays the signal %s s. If it turns off %s times within %s s, it burns out for %s s.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.ticks.observer.w: gives a %s s pulse, %s s after the change.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.ticks.lamp.what: turns on at once and turns off %s s after losing power.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.ticks.dropper.wh: they fire %s s after the signal.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.ticks.buttons.wh: stone ones stay on for %s s and wooden ones for %s s.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.ticks.plates.wha: they stay on for at least %s s (weighted, %s s).
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.ticks.sculk.what: stays on for %s s (calibrated, %s s), then is deaf for %s s.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.crafter.screen: Its screen, set for a chest, with the centre slot disabled.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.crafter.machine: In the simplest use, a hopper fills it, the button gives the signal and the result ends up in the chest.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.crafter.disabled: Nothing goes in, so it stays empty, as the recipe needs.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.crafter.how.1: The crafter has no memory: its recipe is whatever is in its grid right now, placed as on a crafting table. Right-click it to see the 3×3 grid; a hopper fills it slot by slot, left to right and top to bottom.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.crafter.how.2: So tell it where nothing goes: click an empty slot to disable it (it greys out). Disable every slot your recipe leaves empty, like the chest's centre here; another click turns it back on.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.crafter.how.3: A comparator placed against it counts slots: one for each slot that holds an item or is disabled. Once the recipe is complete every slot counts, so it reads %s, whatever the recipe.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.crafter.how.4: A redstone signal makes it craft once, %s s later: it spends 1 item from each slot and the result comes out of its front (the face that looked at you when you placed it). One pulse is one craft: the signal has to turn off before the next.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.crafter.iron: Example: iron blocks on their own
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.crafter.iron.int: The goal is to put iron ingots in a hopper and collect iron blocks from a chest, without touching anything else. The trick is to make the crafter wait until all 9 slots are full.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.crafter.iron.ste: Place the crafter with its front towards a chest, and put a hopper on top. Disable nothing, because an iron block fills all 9 slots.
Put a comparator against its back, so that the end with two small torches touches the crafter. Its signal now tells how many slots are taken.
Lay exactly %s dust from the comparator round to a block stuck to the crafter. The last dust must point into that block, which passes the signal on. Put no dust beside the comparator.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.crafter.iron.why: It must be exactly %s because the signal loses 1 with each dust, and each ingot adds 1 at the comparator. With 8 ingots, the signal runs out before the last dust and nothing happens. The ninth ingot makes 9, which reaches the last dust with 1 left, and that is enough. It matters because 1 ingot alone is already a recipe (9 nuggets), so a signal arriving any earlier would turn your ingots into nuggets.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.crafter.iron.cyc: The craft empties all 9 slots, the comparator falls to 0 and the signal turns off, ready for the next block. A hopper passes 1 item every %s s, so you get 1 block every %s s.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.crafter.gold.int: These are two recipes in a row, nuggets into ingots and ingots into blocks. A crafter facing another crafter puts the result straight into it, one item at a time, with no hopper in between.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.crafter.gold.ste: Place two crafters in a row: the first with its front towards the second, the second with its front towards a chest. The hopper goes on the first.
Give the first the iron machine's circuit, with its comparator, its %s dust and its block. Every 9 nuggets now become 1 ingot inside the second crafter.
Give the second a circuit of its own, also of %s dust. Its back is taken, so the comparator goes against its side.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.crafter.gold.res: Each crafter waits for its own 9, so %s nuggets become 1 gold block in %s s, all through one hopper. The second needs its own circuit for the same reason as iron, because 1 ingot alone would turn back into nuggets.
Disable what the recipe leaves empty. Filled slots plus disabled slots always add up to %s, so the dust line works as it is. For a chest, disable the centre and feed it planks.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.crafter.tip.inco: If the grid makes nothing, a signal only gets a click from the crafter, and the items stay where they are.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.crafter.tip.unde: A hopper under a crafter pulls the ingredients out. The ones that fill it go on top or at its sides.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.crafter.tip.fast: A second hopper on a free side doubles the pace to 1 block every %s s, and nothing jams, because spare items wait in their slot for the next craft.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.crafter.tip.orde: Items take the first free slot, so feed them in that order. For torches, leave only the top-centre and centre slots enabled, and feed coal, then stick. If you do it the other way round, it clicks and stays stuck until you empty it.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.crafter.tip.comp: One comparator reads the crafter. Another reads a spare crafter with all its slots disabled, which always gives %s, and brings it to the first one's side. So the first gives a signal only when the crafter is full, because with fewer the side is stronger. Its signal runs through 3 dust to a target block next to the crafter, which powers it. The comparators stay as placed. With one hopper a block comes out every %s s, with two every %s s.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.build.quasi_conn: A redstone block diagonally above a piston powers the spot over it. The piston counts as powered (in Java), but it does nothing yet.
Any block update next to it (a block placed, a button) makes it push. Dispensers and droppers do the same.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.build.strong_and: Strong power is what a lever or button gives the block it's on, and a repeater or comparator the block it points into. That block powers dust and components around it.
Weak power is what dust gives the block it points into. That block powers lamps, pistons and repeaters around it, but not dust.
A torch strongly powers the block above it, never the block it's on.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.build.transparen: Dust climbs glass and upside-down slabs or stairs, so the signal goes up.
Powered from the top, the signal doesn't come down, so the lower dust stays dark.
Glass over the lower dust doesn't cut the climb; a solid block there would.
Glass carries no power, so a lever on it lights nothing beside it.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.transparency.lis: Transparent blocks carry no power, and the signal climbs them but never comes down
Solid blocks carry power, and the signal goes up and down
The ones with dust drawn on top can hold dust. Leaves, honey and bottom halves hold none.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.build.sticky_blo: Place a sticky piston facing up with a slime block on it. Beside the slime, put a wooden block on its own support. A lever works it.
The slime goes up and takes the wood along, because it drags every normal block it touches, floor and walls too.
Honey on the other side stays (the wood still goes), because slime and honey don't stick to each other.
Glazed terracotta stays, because it only moves when pushed head-on.
A pumpkin stays whole, because it only breaks when a moving block runs into it.
With obsidian on top of the slime, nothing moves, not even the wood. Beside the slime, it would just stay.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.sticky.column.dr: Does it stick to slime or honey?
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.sticky.group.imm: Immovable, and most blocks with an inventory
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.sticky.drag.same: Only by its own kind: slime doesn't take honey, nor honey slime
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.sticky.note.limi: A piston moves %s blocks at most, dragged ones included. With one more, nothing moves.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.sticky.note.floo: Slime and honey drag the floor and walls they touch too, so keep air, or blocks that aren't dragged, around them.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.build.vertical_s: A dust staircase on solid blocks carries the signal up and down.
A zigzag of upside-down slabs (or glass) only takes the signal up, and it is two blocks wide.
A torch tower only takes the signal up, and each torch flips it. With two here, the lamp follows the lever.
A column of observers takes the signal up, or down if you turn them over. They only pass on %s s pulses.
A sculk sensor needs no wire at all. It hears the lever up to %s blocks away, in any direction.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.build.observer_c: Place an observer. Its back, the side with the red dot, gives the pulse.
Place a second observer facing it, and each will see the other change.
It runs by itself and gives a %s s pulse every %s s. Break one to stop it.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.build.repeater_c: Place four repeaters set to 4 clicks in a loop, with dust at the corners.
Place a button next to the loop.
Press once and the pulse runs round for good, on for %s s and off for %s s. The loop must last longer than the button's %s s, or it stays on.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.build.hopper_clo: Place two hoppers feeding each other, and a comparator out of each one into a block.
On the comparators, place sticky pistons facing each other. Put a redstone block over one hopper, and dust on the outer blocks.
Put items in a hopper. They flow across and back, and the block swaps sides each time. Each item adds %s s to a cycle, so %s items give %s s.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.build.t_flip_flo: Place a copper bulb and a button. Each pulse toggles the bulb.
A comparator reads the bulb and gives %s while it is lit, or 0 when it is off.
The first press turns it on and the next turns it off. Any pulse works, from a button, observer or pressure plate.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.build.pulse_limi: Place an observer watching a lever.
Behind it, place a sticky piston with a block.
Each flip gives one %s s pulse. With a pulse that short, a sticky piston drops its block, and the next flip takes it back.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.build.pulse_exte: Place three comparators in a loop, with dust at the corners and along one side.
Place a button into the loop and a lamp under the side dust, which is the output.
When you press, the signal goes round, fading a little each lap. The lamp stays on %s s after the button.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.build.item_sorte: Place a chest fed by a hopper. Above it goes a filter hopper pointing sideways, and on top, a hopper line.
Place a comparator reading the filter, dust on two blocks, then dust one block lower.
That dust powers a block, a repeater, then the block holding a torch that locks the bottom hopper.
In the filter, put %s of the item in slot 1 and 1 junk item in each other slot, which gives signal %s. One more makes %s, and the bottom hopper takes it. Renamed junk is safest.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.build.auto_dropp: Place the dropper facing where items should go (a chest or a water stream), with a hopper on top to fill it.
Behind it, place a comparator reading the dropper, in subtract mode (right-click), then a repeater.

Run 4 dust from the repeater round to a target block next to the dropper. The last dust also touches the comparator's side. While items are left, the circuit switches on and off by itself and the dropper drops one every %s s, the hopper's pace. Empty, it stops.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.build.nether_roo: Ladder and pearl · on top at Y %s

Find a wall under the roof and put ladders on it up to the bedrock. Climb to the top: your head is right under the bedrock, with your feet 2 blocks below the lowest bedrock above you. If the roof starts at Y %s, you are at Y %s.

Keep holding forward against the wall, look at the corner where the bedrock meets the wall and throw the pearl. If it works, you appear on top of the roof, walking at Y %s. Keep 2-block-high gaps away, because the pearl can drop you into them. Java only.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.build.bedrock_in: Efficiency V and Haste II, no TNT
Place a piston on the bedrock facing up, with a redstone torch beside it, so the piston extends.

With lag (for example, a lever surrounded by lots of redstone dust, flicked very fast), break the torch, break the piston and place another in the same spot while looking up, so it faces the bedrock. All three must happen in the same tick.
The new piston does the old one's pending retraction and removes the block it faces: the bedrock. If it fails, try again with more lag.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.build.bedrock_tn: Place a piston on the bedrock facing sideways, with obsidian on top. On the other side, a trapdoor to crawl under. Leave a gap in front of the piston and put the TNT after it. One lever next to the piston and one next to the TNT.
Crawl under the trapdoor and flick both levers: the piston extends and the TNT is lit. Hold another piston, aim at the underside of the obsidian and click nonstop.
The blast breaks the lever and the piston in a random order. If the lever goes first, your new piston is placed facing down and removes the bedrock. If not, build it again.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.farm.space.what: It's the width × width × height it takes to spawn, centred on a block (it is %s wide and %s high).
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.farm.common.dark: block light must be %s, so keep every torch away. Under an opaque roof that hides the sky they spawn day and night. Where skylight reaches (open air, or near a roof's edge), they spawn only at night or in a thunderstorm.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.farm.common.dist: put the spawning floors %s to %s blocks from where you wait (AFK). Any closer and nothing spawns; any farther and they vanish at once. Past %s they also vanish little by little, so get them to the kill area fast.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.farm.common.cap: there can be %s monsters at most. Every unnamed one in the chunks within %s blocks of you counts, including those still in your farm. Dark caves use up that limit, so light up or fill the caves around you, or build over the ocean or high in the sky.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.farm.mob_farm.fl: they need a block with a full solid top, and top slabs work. Glass, leaves, ice and bottom slabs don't. The spawning space can't hold a button, pressure plate, rail, redstone dust or water.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.farm.mob_farm.ro: measured centred on a block, and the block above the feet can't be a full block. To keep spiders out, make the floors 2 wide.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.farm.mob_farm.he: each try picks a height at random between the world's bottom and the column's top block, and the group spawns at that height. So the more floors you stack, the more tries land in your farm.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.farm.spawner.pla: a player within %s blocks of it (a sphere).
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.farm.spawner.are: they spawn in %s×%s, 3 high, which means up to %s blocks on each side and from 1 below to 1 above the spawner.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.farm.spawner.roo: they need no floor, because they spawn wherever they fit, even in the air.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.farm.spawner.rat: it makes %s tries a cycle, then waits %s–%s s at random.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.farm.spawner.cap: it stops while %s of its mobs are in the %s×%s×%s box around it, so move them out.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.farm.spawner.lig: zombies, skeletons and spiders need block light 0 and no daylight (underground, always). One torch stops it. Blazes need light %s or less.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.farm.iron_farm.v: %s villagers within %s blocks of each other that slept in a bed in the last %s min. So each one needs a wool bed it can reach, and to sleep in it at night. No workstation or bell is needed.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.farm.iron_farm.s: a zombie within %s blocks that a villager can see (glass hides it) scares it, and a scared villager tries to call a golem every %s s. Without a scare, %s villagers gossiping manage it now and then.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.farm.iron_farm.c: after a golem spawns, or while they sense one within %s blocks (even through walls), they wait %s s. So take golems away or kill them fast.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.farm.iron_farm.s: it spawns in a %s×%s×%s box around the scared villager, with %s tries. Each try goes down a random column and looks for the first solid block with air or water above and %s blocks free. It can't spawn on glass, leaves, ice, glowstone, sea lanterns or bottom slabs.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.farm.breeder.foo: both parents need %s food points each, which is %s bread, or %s carrots, potatoes or beetroots. They eat it when breeding. Throw it to them, because they pick it up.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.farm.breeder.par: two awake adults that see each other, within %s blocks. They don't need a profession.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.farm.breeder.bed: they need a free bed, meaning one no villager has claimed. It must be wool, not straw, within %s blocks, with %s blocks of air above it and a path they can walk. With a block right over the pillow, or just 1 free over the whole bed, they can sleep but no baby comes. If the bed is enclosed with just 1 free, they suffocate on waking. Each baby keeps one bed, so with no free bed there is no baby.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.farm.breeder.whe: they breed only in their free time, by day (%s min). With no workstation or bell, they have all of it. With a workstation, they have only %s s at dawn and %s s before bed, plus %s s if there's no bell.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.farm.breeder.tim: they spend %s–%s s together. The parents then wait %s min, and the baby grows up in %s min.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.farm.raid_farm.s: drink an ominous bottle, which gives Bad Omen for %s min, and step into a village. You get Raid Omen, and %s s later the raid starts there.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.farm.raid_farm.v: a village is any spot within one section (a %s-block cube) of a bed, workstation or bell a villager has claimed, so one villager with its bed is enough. If they die or lose those blocks, the raid is lost. It doesn't work in the Nether.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.farm.raid_farm.c: the raid's centre is the average of those claimed blocks within %s blocks of where it started. Waves spawn on top of each column's highest block, outside the village, so your spawning floor must be the highest thing around.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.farm.raid_farm.w: there are %s waves on Easy, %s on Normal and %s on Hard, plus one with Bad Omen II or more. Each one comes %s s after the last raider of the one before dies.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.farm.raid_farm.s: a raider more than %s blocks from the centre drops out. A raid ends after %s min.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.farm.witch_hut.b: they spawn only inside the hut's box, which is %s wide, %s long and %s high from one block below its floor. Build your spawning floors inside it.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.farm.witch_hut.o: every monster that spawns in the box is a witch, on your floors too.
they spawn in 1 chunk in %s, set by the seed (find it with a slime chunk finder), below Y %s, in any light. There, only 1 try in %s goes on.
in swamps they spawn from Y %s to %s, in light %s or less. Half the tries count at full moon, and none at new moon.
every size, even the small ones, needs the big one's room (%s), which is 3×3 and 3 high.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.farm.guardian_fa: they spawn anywhere in the monument's box (%s×%s, Y %s–%s). Inside it, every monster is a guardian.
water with water below it, and no floor is needed. Where the sky can be seen from the water, only 1 try in %s goes on, so covered water spawns far more.
any light works. Elder guardians never come back.
tries pick a height between the world's bottom and the surface, and only those landing between Y %s and %s count.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.farm.wither_farm: inside the box of any fortress piece (table below) any floor a mob can spawn on works. Between pieces, but inside the box around the whole fortress, only plain nether bricks work, not slabs, stairs or other bricks.
put wither roses on grass, dirt or netherrack. Only the wither skeleton can spawn inside a rose, because it's the one fortress mob they don't hurt. Where there's no rose, the others spawn too.
of every %s, there are %s blazes, %s wither skeletons, %s zombified piglins, %s magma cubes and %s skeletons.
wither skeletons and skeletons need light %s or less, blazes and zombified piglins %s or less, and magma cubes any.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.farm.fortress.ti: Fortress pieces: any floor works inside their box
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.farm.fortress.no: "Below floor" is how many blocks of the box lie under the level you stand on, and "above floor" the levels from there up, that one included. A mob counts when its feet are inside the box of some piece, so you can dig or build within those limits. The pillars under the bridges are outside. The plan follows the piece: the first number is its width, the second its length.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.farm.enderman_fa: they spawn in any End biome, in groups of up to %s.
they need block light 0. The End has no day or night, so the time doesn't matter.
they go for an endermite they see within %s blocks. Put one in a minecart and name it, because otherwise it vanishes after %s min.
they spawn in basalt deltas, where they're most of the monsters, and a few in fortresses and nether wastes.
every size, even the small ones, needs the big one's room (%s), which is 3×3 and 3 high.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.farm.gold_farm.c: each portal block, each random tick, has 1 chance on Easy, 2 on Normal and 3 on Hard out of %s.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.farm.gold_farm.w: only Overworld portals work. They spawn on the block under the portal (its bottom frame) if a monster can stand there, even with no room.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.farm.gold_farm.p: a player within %s blocks, not on Peaceful, with the portal within simulation distance. The monster cap doesn't stop it.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.farm.gold_farm.s: the bigger the portal, the more spawn, up to %s×%s inside.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.farm.drowned_far: they spawn in water with water below it, in river, ocean or dripstone cave biomes. In unfrozen rivers, 1 try in %s goes on. In oceans and dripstone caves, 1 in %s does, and only below Y %s.
cheatsheet.tab.redstone.farm.shulker_far: Bullet hits an open shulker = one more
shulkers fire a bullet that chases its target and hits the first thing it touches. They aim at players they can see within %s blocks and at whatever attacks them, except other shulkers.
if the bullet hits another shulker that's open, that one teleports away and a new one of the same colour appears right where it was. Closed, it only takes the damage.

no teleport means no copy. The shulker tries %s random spots up to %s blocks away on each axis. Each spot must be air, next to a solid block (not bedrock), with the next block free so it can open. If none works, nothing happens. The new one needs no room of its own, because it uses the one left behind.

it then counts the shulkers within %s blocks on each axis of the spot it left, itself included but not the new one. If it's alone, it always copies. Each extra shulker takes off %s%%, and with %s or more it never copies. The shooter counts too if it's that close.
if the hit leaves it below half health, 1 time in %s it only teleports, with no copy. The new one is born with full health.
they don't spawn on their own, but come with End cities. To take one, push a boat or minecart into it and it gets in.
config.cheatsheet.title: Cheat Sheet
config.cheatsheet.group.cheat_sheet.desc: How you open the cheat sheet and which tab it shows first.
config.cheatsheet.pause_button.descripti: Shows a book button in the row of small icon buttons of the pause menu that opens the cheat sheet.
config.cheatsheet.start_tab.description: The tab the cheat sheet opens on: the one you were reading last time, or always the same one.
config.cheatsheet.sheet_scale.descriptio: How big the cheat sheet is drawn, apart from the game's GUI scale. Auto makes it as big as possible while the whole tab still fits on screen; a number draws it at that size.
config.cheatsheet.confirm_command_delete: Asks you to confirm before deleting one of your saved commands. If you ticked “Don't ask me again”, turn this back on to get the question back.
config.cheatsheet.group.keys.description: The same bindings as Options → Controls. Changes apply when you save.
config.cheatsheet.key.description: Click, then press a key or mouse button. Escape unbinds it.
config.cheatsheet.cancel.tooltip: Forgets pending changes and closes the settings.
config.cheatsheet.reset.tooltip: Resets all options to default. (This can be undone!)
config.cheatsheet.undo.tooltip: Reverts all options to what they were before editing.
